subject: Request: Rate-tier carveout & fairness override for PeakPilot launch
messages:
From: Tim Barnes <tim@peakpilot.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: operations@peakpilot.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Launch week capacity ask — temporary rate-tier carveout

Hi Lauren,

We expect a major product launch the week of Sep 6 with a concentrated 72-hour spike. Early forecasts (attached) show a 9x increase in peak QPS for our chat endpoint vs. baseline. Our legal and ops teams are comfortable with standard redaction and retention controls but we need a temporary increase in burst allowance and a fairness-policy carveout for that window to avoid throttling that would materially affect customer experience.

Specific ask:
- Temporary burst ceiling: +6x on our reserved quota for 72 hours;
- Short-lived fairness override so our traffic isn’t deprioritized when other tenants have short bursts;
- Confirmation of fallbacks (model-variant downgrade / graceful 429 strategy) we can implement if capacity still constrained.

Attached: PeakPilot_traffic_forecast.csv, high-level launch timeline.

Can we get a list of the options (technical + commercial) and an estimated cost uplift by EOD Friday? We’re under a hard launch timeline and would prefer to keep this within our Dedicated contract if possible.

Thanks,
Tim Barnes
Head of Ops, PeakPilot

---
Note: This message thread was sent to lauren's inbox for coordination on the exception request.

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Barnes <tim@peakpilot.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch week capacity ask — temporary rate-tier carveout

Tim — thanks for the heads up and the forecast. We can work this, but there are a few moving parts to confirm. High level options from our side: 

1) Short-term dedicated burst: Promote a capped burst pool (6x for 72h) on your Dedicated tenant. Requires a one-time operational uplift and a short policy exception.
2) Fairness override window: We can apply a time-boxed priority lane (2–3 hour rolling windows) instead of a global override — safer from a multi-tenant fairness perspective.
3) Graceful degradation plan: Auto-fallback to a smaller model family (fewer tokens/resolution) + adaptive rate-limiter that returns informative 429s with Retry-After headers when thresholds are hit.

I’ve looped in Karthik to confirm the runtime implications and Marissa for commercial approval on a temporary uplift fee. If Legal needs to sign off on the exception we can route the SLA-exception-form.pdf through DocuSign.

Next steps: Karthik — can you confirm whether a 6x burst is feasible without DB/KV pressure and estimate expected latency delta? Marissa — can you provide a ballpark uplift % and whether we can do a capped credit vs. itemized overage?

Tim — if you can share exact launch UTC windows (start/end) we’ll draft the exception and a rollback plan.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: SLA-exception-form.pdf

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Tim Barnes <tim@peakpilot.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 13:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch week capacity ask — temporary rate-tier carveout

Lauren / Tim — quick technical readout:

- Feasibility: We can provision a time-limited burst pool attached to PeakPilot's Dedicated capacity. 6x for 72 hours is achievable if the peak is spread across at least a few availability zones; single-AZ concentrated spikes increase risk.
- Latency: Expect median token latency to remain within SLA for the standard model. Under peak sustained concurrency we should plan for 12–30% p95 latency increase on the largest prompts; smaller prompts unaffected.
- Fairness policy: We prefer a controlled priority lane (rate-window token bank) rather than a blanket fairness disable; it gives us predictable isolation and simpler rollback.
- Operational tasks: provisioning, temporary routing rule, alerting, and a canary ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100% traffic over 2 hours). We’ll need an ops on-call window during the launch.

I’ll attach a short runbook snippet in the Drive link. If PeakPilot can agree to the canary ramp and AZ distribution we can proceed.

—Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Barnes <tim@peakpilot.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2027 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch week capacity ask — temporary rate-tier carveout

Approving commercial approach with conditions:

- Pricing: I can approve a capped uplift of +30% over their monthly committed spend for the 72h window (no surprise invoices). If PeakPilot prefers itemized overage billing we’ll need CFO sign-off.
- Credit vs. charge: Offer a one-time promotional credit to cover up to 50% of uplift if they commit to a 6-month minimum reserved capacity increase post-launch.
- Legal: We will not change the core SLA; exception covers only rate-tier/fairness policy for the specified time-boxed window. Legal needs to sign the exception form.

Ben, coordinate with finance to draft the quote and with contracts on the DocuSign flow. Lauren — please get the exact UTC launch windows and confirm AZ distribution from PeakPilot.

Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Barnes <tim@peakpilot.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, PeakPilot Legal <legal@peakpilot.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Launch week capacity ask — temporary rate-tier carveout

Tim — thanks. Confirmed items below and next steps: 

1) We will provision a time-limited burst pool (6x) for 72 hours starting Sep 6 00:00:00 UTC to Sep 8 23:59:59 UTC. This requires: AZ distribution across at least two zones (you confirmed this in the attached traffic file).
2) Fairness: We’ll apply a controlled priority lane (rolling 3-hour windows) as the safe override; full global fairness disable is not permitted.
3) Canary plan: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 hours at start of window with ops on-call (Karthik will kick this off).
4) Commercials: +30% capped uplift for the window. We’ll offer a promotional credit covering 50% of uplift if you commit to increasing reserved capacity for 6 months. Ben will send the quote and DocuSign link.
5) Legal sign-off: Please have your legal team sign the SLA-exception-form.pdf. I’ve attached a DocuSign link in related_links.

Attached: SLA-exception-form.pdf (for signature), PeakPilot_traffic_forecast.csv

If all good I’ll route the DocuSign and schedule the ops runbook review meeting for Aug 25.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference
